# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

- oAuth2 authentication.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/authorize](https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token](https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|block.read|View accounts you have blocked.|
|block.write|Block and unblock accounts on your behalf.|
|bookmark.read|Read your bookmarked Posts.|
|bookmark.write|Create and delete your bookmarks.|
|broadcast.read|View your live broadcasts and their chat.|
|broadcast.write|Manage your live broadcasts and send chat messages on your behalf.|
|calls.join|Join X calls for you, and listen, speak, send chat messages, and admit people who ask to join.|
|calls.read|View your X calls and the calls on your calendar.|
|calls.write|Start, schedule, change, and cancel X calls for you, and answer invitations.|
|developer.read|View your developer accounts, apps, and settings.|
|developer.write|Create and manage your X Developer Platform account.|
|dm.read|Read all your Direct Messages.|
|dm.write|Send and manage your Direct Messages.|
|follows.read|View accounts you follow and accounts following you.|
|follows.write|Follow and unfollow accounts on your behalf.|
|like.read|View Posts you have liked and likes you can see.|
|like.write|Like and unlike Posts on your behalf.|
|list.read|View Lists, members, and followers of Lists you created or are a member of, including private Lists.|
|list.write|Create and manage Lists on your behalf.|
|media.write|Upload media, such as photos and videos, on your behalf.|
|mute.read|View accounts you have muted.|
|mute.write|Mute and unmute accounts on your behalf.|
|offline.access|Request a refresh token for the app.|
|saved_search.read|View your saved searches.|
|saved_search.write|Create and delete saved searches for you.|
|settings.read|View your account settings.|
|settings.write|Change your account settings for you.|
|space.read|View all Spaces you have access to.|
|timeline.read|View all Custom Timelines you can see.|
|tweet.moderate.write|Hide and unhide replies to your posts.|
|tweet.read|View all posts you can see, including those from protected accounts.|
|tweet.write|Create and repost on your behalf.|
|users.read|View any account you can see, including protected accounts.|
|users.write|Update your profile, including your name, bio, profile image, and banner.|

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: oauth

<h1 id="x-api-v2-account">Account</h1>

Endpoints for managing the authenticated user's X Developer Platform account

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/introduction">Find out more</a>

## Get developer account

<a id="opIdgetDeveloperAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/account \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/account`

Returns the authenticated user's X Developer Platform account. A user without an account gets a resource-not-found error entry.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "account_id": "string",
    "created_at": "string",
    "name": "string"
  },
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",
      "parameter": "string",
      "resource_id": "string",
      "resource_type": "string",
      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-developer-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[GetDeveloperAccountResponse](#schemagetdeveloperaccountresponse)|
|default|Default|The request has failed.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2UserToken ( Scopes: developer.read )
</aside>

## Ensure developer account

<a id="opIdensureAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/account \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "metadata": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /2/account`

Creates an X Developer Platform account for the authenticated user if they do not already have one, and returns it. Idempotent: when the user already has an account it is returned unchanged with `created` false.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "metadata": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="ensure-developer-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[EnsureAccountRequest](#schemaensureaccountrequest)|true|none|
|» metadata|body|string|false|Optional provisioning-credit metadata (an opaque string, e.g. a subscription tier) to claim for the account, attributed to the calling app. Omit to just ensure the account.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "account_id": "string",
    "created": true
  },
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",
      "parameter": "string",
      "resource_id": "string",
      "resource_type": "string",
      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="ensure-developer-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[EnsureAccountResponse](#schemaensureaccountresponse)|
|default|Default|The request has failed.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2UserToken ( Scopes: developer.write )
</aside>

## Create X activity subscription

<a id="opIdcreateActivitySubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/activity/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "event_type": "profile.update.bio",
    "expires_at": "string",
    "filter": {
      "direction": "inbound",
      "keyword": "string",
      "qualifiers": {},
      "user_id": "string"
    },
    "tag": "string",
    "webhook_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /2/activity/subscriptions`

Creates a subscription for an X activity event. OAuth2 user-context tokens must hold the scope matching the requested event_type: dm.read for chat.* and dm.* events, like.read for like.* events, mute.read for mute.* events, block.read for block.* events, follows.read for subscriptions.* events, and tweet.read for all other event types. Mute and block subscriptions are actor-only: filter.user_id must identify the authenticated user and direction is not supported. subscriptions.* events require a user-context token and filter.user_id must identify the authenticated user. Optional filter.qualifiers further narrow supported chat, follow, unfollow, like, and subscriptions events.

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/activity/create-x-activity-subscription">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_type": "profile.update.bio",
  "expires_at": "string",
  "filter": {
    "direction": "inbound",
    "keyword": "string",
    "qualifiers": {},
    "user_id": "string"
  },
  "tag": "string",
  "webhook_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-x-activity-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateActivitySubscriptionRequest](#schemacreateactivitysubscriptionrequest)|true|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|Activity event type in dot notation. `chat.conversation_join` is a deprecated alias of `chat.conversation.join`; responses always use the canonical name.|
|» expires_at|body|string|false|Optional RFC 3339 expiration time. Re-creating the same subscription refreshes this value; omitting it makes the subscription permanent.|
|» filter|body|[CreateActivitySubscriptionFilter](#schemacreateactivitysubscriptionfilter)|true|Subscription filter.|
|» tag|body|string|false|Optional caller-defined tag.|
|» webhook_id|body|string|false|Webhook to deliver the subscription events to.|

|---|---|
|» event_type|profile.update.bio|
|» event_type|profile.update.profile_picture|

## Create a bot

<a id="opIdcreateBot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/bots \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "display_name": "string",
    "handle": "string",
    "scopes": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /2/bots`

Creates a bot account in the calling app's project and returns its bearer token. Idempotent on handle: repeating the request for a handle that already names one of the project's bots returns that bot with a freshly minted token, revoking the previous one — safe to retry when a response was lost, since the replaced token was never seen.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "display_name": "string",
  "handle": "string",
  "scopes": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-bot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateBotRequest](#schemacreatebotrequest)|true|none|
|» display_name|body|string|false|The bot's display name; defaults to the handle.|
|» handle|body|string|true|The bot's handle (X screen name): 5-15 characters, letters, numbers, or underscores.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|Scopes for the bot's bearer token. Broadcast moderation additionally supports broadcast.read and broadcast.write. Defaults to the XChat scope set (dm.read, dm.write, tweet.read, users.read, media.write).|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "scopes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "token": "string",
    "token_expires_at_ms": 0,
    "username": "string"
  },
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",
      "parameter": "string",
      "resource_id": "string",
      "resource_type": "string",
      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-bot-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The request has succeeded.|[CreateBotResponse](#schemacreatebotresponse)|
|default|Default|The request has failed.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BearerToken
</aside>

## List broadcasts

<a id="opIdlistBroadcasts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/broadcasts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/broadcasts`

Returns the authenticated user's live-video broadcasts, or selected owned broadcasts when ids are provided.

At most one of `ids`, `max_results` may be provided. At most one of `ids`, `pagination_token` may be provided.

<h3 id="list-broadcasts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|ids|query|[string]|false|Comma-separated broadcast IDs to retrieve instead of listing broadcasts.|
|max_results|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|pagination_token|query|string|false|none|
|broadcast.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Broadcast fields to display.|

## Add a chat moderator

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/broadcasts/chat/moderators \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
```

`POST /2/broadcasts/chat/moderators`

## Create a scheduled broadcast

<a id="opIdcreateScheduledBroadcast"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/broadcasts/scheduled \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "available_for_replay": true,
    "chat_option": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "is_locked": true,
    "locale": "string",
    "manual_publish": true,
    "recurrence": {
      "frequency": "Daily",
      "repeats": "string"
    },
    "scheduled_end_ms": "string",
    "scheduled_start_ms": "string",
    "source_id": "string",
    "telecast_id": "string",
    "thumbnail_media_id": "string",
    "title": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /2/broadcasts/scheduled`

Schedules a broadcast for the authenticated user. A `source_id` (ingest) is required at create time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "available_for_replay": true,
  "chat_option": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "is_locked": true,
  "locale": "string",
  "manual_publish": true,
  "recurrence": {
    "frequency": "Daily",
    "repeats": "string"
  },
  "scheduled_end_ms": "string",
  "scheduled_start_ms": "string",
  "source_id": "string",
  "telecast_id": "string",
  "thumbnail_media_id": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-scheduled-broadcast-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateScheduledBroadcastRequest](#schemacreatescheduledbroadcastrequest)|true|none|
|» available_for_replay|body|boolean|false|Enable replay.|
|» chat_option|body|string|false|Who can chat (numeric string): `0` default, `1` chat off, `2` everyone, `3` verified accounts, `4` accounts the host follows, `5` the host's subscribers, `6` accounts followed by an account the host follows.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description.|
|» is_locked|body|boolean|false|Lock the broadcast.|
|» locale|body|string|false|Locale.|
|» manual_publish|body|boolean|false|If true, do not auto-publish at start; call POST .../live when ready.|
|» recurrence|body|[CreateScheduledBroadcastRecurrence](#schemacreatescheduledbroadcastrecurrence)|false|Deprecated: recurring schedules are being retired and requests that include `recurrence` will be rejected. Create each occurrence as its own scheduled broadcast.|
|» scheduled_end_ms|body|string|false|Optional end time, ms since Unix epoch (decimal string). Omit for an open-ended broadcast.|
|» scheduled_start_ms|body|string|true|Start time, ms since Unix epoch (decimal string).|
|» source_id|body|string|true|Ingest / source id to bind (same as sources `rtmp_stream_key`).|
|» telecast_id|body|string|false|Deprecated: telecast associations are being retired and this field will be ignored.|
|» thumbnail_media_id|body|string|false|Pre-live slate media id (numeric string).|
|» title|body|string|false|Title / status text.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "available_for_replay": true,
    "broadcast_id": "string",
    "chat_option": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "locale": "string",
    "manual_publish": true,
    "recurring_schedule_id": "string",
    "scheduled_broadcast_id": "string",
    "scheduled_end_ms": "string",

  },

    {
      "detail": "string",

      "resource_type": "string",
      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

```bash
  }'
```

`PUT /2/broadcasts/scheduled/{id}`

Updates a scheduled broadcast. Path `:id` is the broadcast id; the body must include `scheduled_broadcast_id`. Re-send every field that should be kept.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "available_for_replay": true,
  "chat_option": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "is_locked": true,
  "locale": "string",
  "manual_publish": true,
  "roll_forward": true,
  "scheduled_broadcast_id": "string",
  "scheduled_end_ms": "string",
  "scheduled_start_ms": "string",
  "source_id": "string",
  "thumbnail_media_id": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-scheduled-broadcast-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[UpdateScheduledBroadcastRequest](#schemaupdatescheduledbroadcastrequest)|true|none|
|» available_for_replay|body|boolean|false|Enable replay.|
|» chat_option|body|string|false|Who can chat (numeric string): `0` default, `1` chat off, `2` everyone, `3` verified accounts, `4` accounts the host follows, `5` the host's subscribers, `6` accounts followed by an account the host follows.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description.|
|» is_locked|body|boolean|false|Lock the broadcast.|
|» locale|body|string|false|Locale.|
|» manual_publish|body|boolean|false|If true, do not auto-publish at start; call POST .../live when ready.|
|» roll_forward|body|boolean|false|Deprecated: recurring schedules are being retired and `true` will be rejected.|
|» scheduled_broadcast_id|body|string|true|Numeric scheduler id from create/list/get.|
|» scheduled_end_ms|body|string|true|End time, ms since Unix epoch (decimal string).|
|» scheduled_start_ms|body|string|true|Start time, ms since Unix epoch (decimal string).|
|» source_id|body|string|false|Ingest / source id.|
|» thumbnail_media_id|body|string|false|Pre-live slate media id (numeric string).|
|» title|body|string|false|Title / status text.|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/broadcasts/string/chat \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reply_to": "string",
    "text": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /2/broadcasts/{id}/chat`

Posts a chat message to a running broadcast, attributed to the authenticated user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reply_to": "string",
  "text": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-chat-message-to-a-live-broadcast-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Create a call

<a id="opIdcreateCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "audio_only": true,
    "conversation_id": "string",
    "join_policy": "open",
    "title": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /2/calls`

Starts an X call hosted by the authenticated user (typically a bot). Pass an XChat conversation_id to start the call in that conversation, or omit it for a standalone call anyone can join with the returned join_url (subject to join_policy). The call starts empty: put an agent in it with POST /2/calls/:id/join. When the host joins a conversation call, the other members are rung.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "audio_only": true,
  "conversation_id": "string",
  "join_policy": "open",
  "title": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateCallRequest](#schemacreatecallrequest)|true|none|
|» audio_only|body|boolean|false|Start the call without video.|
|» conversation_id|body|string|false|XChat conversation to start the call in.|
|» join_policy|body|string|false|open (default): anyone with the link joins; closed: the host admits each person; trusted: members of the host's Verified Organization join, others ask.|
|» title|body|string|false|Title shown to participants.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» join_policy|open|
|» join_policy|closed|
|» join_policy|trusted|

## List scheduled calls

<a id="opIdlistScheduledCalls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls/scheduled \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/calls/scheduled`

Returns the X calls on the authenticated user's calendar, earliest first: events on their X Calls calendar, and events on the Microsoft Outlook calendars they linked to X whose conference is an X call. Calls still running at start_time are included. The window defaults to the next 24 hours and may span at most 7 days. Use scheduled_call.fields to select which fields are returned.

When both are provided, `start_time` must be earlier than `end_time`.

<h3 id="list-scheduled-calls-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|Calls still running at this time or starting after it (RFC 3339). Defaults to now.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|Calls starting before this time (RFC 3339). Defaults to 24 hours after start_time.|
|max_results|query|integer(int32)|false|The most calls to return. Defaults to 20.|
|scheduled_call.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of ScheduledCall fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|call.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Call fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|

## Schedule a call

<a id="opIdscheduleCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls/scheduled \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "duration_minutes": 1,
    "invitee_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "notify_invitees": true,
    "recurrence": "string",
    "start_time": "string",
    "time_zone": "string",
    "title": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /2/calls/scheduled`

Puts an X call on the authenticated user's X Calls calendar, with them as its organizer, and invites people to it. The call exists right away: share its join_url, or put an agent in it at start time with POST /2/calls/:id/join. A recurrence (an RFC 5545 RRULE) repeats it. Invitees get an email unless notify_invitees is false.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "duration_minutes": 1,
  "invitee_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "notify_invitees": true,
  "recurrence": "string",
  "start_time": "string",
  "time_zone": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-a-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ScheduleCallRequest](#schemaschedulecallrequest)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|What the call is about.|
|» duration_minutes|body|integer|false|How long the call lasts, in minutes. Defaults to 30; at most 31 days.|
|» invitee_ids|body|[string]|false|X user ids of the people to invite.|
|» notify_invitees|body|boolean|false|Whether invitees get an email about the call. Defaults to true.|
|» recurrence|body|string|false|RFC 5545 RRULE to repeat the call by, such as FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO; the RRULE: prefix is optional.|
|» start_time|body|string|true|When the call starts (RFC 3339); not in the past.|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|IANA time zone the recurrence follows, such as America/Los_Angeles.|
|» title|body|string|false|Title invitees see.|

## Get a scheduled call

<a id="opIdgetScheduledCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls/scheduled/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/calls/scheduled/{id}`

Returns a scheduled call the authenticated user organizes or is invited to, at its occurrence running now or its next one within a year: its time, call, recurrence and who is invited and how they answered. Changes can take a few seconds to show here. Use scheduled_call.fields to select which fields are returned.

<h3 id="get-a-scheduled-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|scheduled_call.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of ScheduledCall fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|call.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Call fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|

## Update a scheduled call

<a id="opIdupdateScheduledCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls/scheduled/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "duration_minutes": 1,
    "invitee_ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "notify_invitees": true,
    "occurrence_start_time": "string",
    "recurrence": "string",
    "scope": "all",
    "start_time": "string",
    "time_zone": "string",
    "title": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /2/calls/scheduled/{id}`

Moves, renames or re-invites a scheduled call the authenticated user organizes. Only the fields sent change. For a recurring call, scope and occurrence_start_time pick the occurrences: all of them (the default), one, or one and every one after it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "duration_minutes": 1,
  "invitee_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "notify_invitees": true,
  "occurrence_start_time": "string",
  "recurrence": "string",
  "scope": "all",
  "start_time": "string",
  "time_zone": "string",
  "title": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-scheduled-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[UpdateScheduledCallRequest](#schemaupdatescheduledcallrequest)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|What the call is about.|
|» duration_minutes|body|integer|false|How long the call lasts, in minutes.|
|» invitee_ids|body|[string]|false|Everyone to invite: replaces the invite list. At most 25 of them may be people not invited yet.|
|» notify_invitees|body|boolean|false|Whether invitees get an email about the change. Defaults to true.|
|» occurrence_start_time|body|string|false|Start of the occurrence that scope this or this_and_following refers to (RFC 3339).|
|» recurrence|body|string|false|RFC 5545 RRULE to repeat the call by, such as FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO.|
|» scope|body|string|false|Which occurrences of a recurring call: all (the default without occurrence_start_time), this (the default with it), or this_and_following.|
|» start_time|body|string|false|When the call (or the chosen occurrence) starts now (RFC 3339).|
|» time_zone|body|string|false|IANA time zone the recurrence follows.|
|» title|body|string|false|Title invitees see.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» scope|all|
|» scope|this|
|» scope|this_and_following|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "updated": true
  },
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",
      "parameter": "string",
      "resource_id": "string",
      "resource_type": "string",
      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Cancel a scheduled call

<a id="opIdcancelScheduledCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls/scheduled/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /2/calls/scheduled/{id}`

Cancels a scheduled call the authenticated user organizes, and takes it off invitees' calendars. For a recurring call, scope and occurrence_start_time pick the occurrences: all of them (the default), one, or one and every one after it. Cancelling what is already cancelled succeeds.

<h3 id="cancel-a-scheduled-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|scope|query|string|false|Which occurrences: all (the default without occurrence_start_time), this (the default with it), or this_and_following.|
|occurrence_start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of the occurrence that scope this or this_and_following refers to (RFC 3339).|
|notify_invitees|query|boolean|false|Whether invitees get an email about it. Defaults to true.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|all|
|scope|this|
|scope|this_and_following|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cancelled": true
  },
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",
      "parameter": "string",
      "resource_id": "string",
      "resource_type": "string",
      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

</aside>

## Respond to a scheduled call

<a id="opIdrespondToScheduledCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls/scheduled/string/rsvp \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "occurrence_start_time": "string",
    "response": "accepted",
    "scope": "all"
  }'
```

`POST /2/calls/scheduled/{id}/rsvp`

Accepts, declines or tentatively accepts an invitation to a scheduled call for the authenticated user. For a recurring call, scope and occurrence_start_time pick the occurrences the answer is for: all of them (the default), one, or one and every one after it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "occurrence_start_time": "string",
  "response": "accepted",
  "scope": "all"
}
```

<h3 id="respond-to-a-scheduled-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[RespondToScheduledCallRequest](#schemarespondtoscheduledcallrequest)|true|none|
|» occurrence_start_time|body|string|false|Start of the occurrence that scope this or this_and_following refers to (RFC 3339).|
|» response|body|string|true|The answer to the invitation.|
|» scope|body|string|false|Which occurrences of a recurring call: all (the default without occurrence_start_time), this (the default with it), or this_and_following.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» response|accepted|
|» response|declined|
|» response|tentative|
|» scope|all|
|» scope|this|
|» scope|this_and_following|

```json
      "status": 0,

    }
  ]
}
```

## Join a call

<a id="opIdjoinCall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/calls/string/join \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "media": {
      "audio": {
        "encoding": "pcm16",
        "sample_rate": 0
      },
      "type": "websocket"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /2/calls/{id}/join`

Starts a media session that takes part in the call as the authenticated user. The response carries a media_url and a short-lived media_token: open a WebSocket to media_url with the token as a Bearer credential to exchange PCM16 audio and events with the call; the user enters the call when the WebSocket connects. On a closed or trusted call the session asks the host first (admission: requires_approval).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "media": {
    "audio": {
      "encoding": "pcm16",
      "sample_rate": 0
    },
    "type": "websocket"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="join-a-call-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[JoinCallRequest](#schemajoincallrequest)|true|none|
|» media|body|[JoinCallMedia](#schemajoincallmedia)|false|The media session to start.|

## Get Chat Conversations; unread state via chat_conversation.fields=unread,last_read_event_id,newest_event_id

<a id="opIdgetChatConversations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/chat/conversations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/chat/conversations`

Retrieves a list of Chat conversations for the authenticated user's inbox. The unread, last_read_event_id and newest_event_id fields give your read state, computed from your latest read receipt and each conversation's latest notifying message. With unread_only=true, only conversations that are unread for you are returned; a page can then hold fewer than max_results, so keep paging while has_more is true.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-chat-conversations-unread-state-via-chatconversationfieldsunreadlastreadeventidnewesteventid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|max_results|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|pagination_token|query|string|false|none|
|unread_only|query|boolean|false|Return only unread conversations. A page can be short; keep paging while has_more.|
|chat_conversation.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of ChatConversation fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|

## Get Chat Conversation; unread state via chat_conversation.fields=unread,last_read_event_id,newest_event_id

<a id="opIdgetChatConversation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/chat/conversations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/chat/conversations/{id}`

Returns metadata for a Chat conversation including type, muted status, and group details. Use chat_conversation.fields to select which fields are returned. Use expansions to hydrate member, admin, or participant user objects. Use user.fields to control which profile fields are returned for expanded users. The unread, last_read_event_id and newest_event_id fields give your read state, computed from your latest read receipt and the conversation's latest notifying message.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-chat-conversation-unread-state-via-chatconversationfieldsunreadlastreadeventidnewesteventid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|chat_conversation.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of ChatConversation fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|

`PUT /2/chat/conversations/{id}`

Renames an encrypted Chat group conversation, changes its avatar, or sets its description. The client encrypts each value with the conversation key and lists the values it changed in modified_fields.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

|body|body|[UpdateChatGroupRequest](#schemaupdatechatgrouprequest)|true|none|

## Delete a Chat conversation

<a id="opIddeleteChatConversation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/chat/conversations/string \
```

`DELETE /2/chat/conversations/{id}`

Deletes a Chat conversation for the authenticated user only; other participants keep it. Works for group and 1:1 conversations. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient. Deleting a pending message request's conversation deletes the request, like Delete in the X app.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action_signatures": [

            "public_key_version": "string",
            "signing_public_key": "string"
          }
        ],

        "signature": "string",
        "signature_version": "string",
        "signing_public_key": "string"
      },
      "message_id": "string",
      "signature_payload": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the conversation: a group ID starting with `g`, the other user's ID for a 1:1 conversation, or both user IDs of a 1:1 conversation joined by a hyphen.|
|body|body|[DeleteChatConversationRequest](#schemadeletechatconversationrequest)|true|none|

## Get pending admin requests for a Chat group conversation

<a id="opIdgetChatGroupAdminRequests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/chat/conversations/{id}/admin_requests`

Returns the users who have asked to become admins of an encrypted Chat group conversation. Only a group admin can list admin requests. Use user.fields to select which profile fields are returned.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|id|path|string|true|The ID of the group conversation, starting with `g`.|
|pagination_token|query|string|false|The next_token from a previous response, to fetch the next page.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|

`PUT /2/chat/conversations/{id}/admin_settings`

Sets which actions only admins can perform in an existing encrypted Chat group conversation. A setting set to true restricts that action to admins, and false opens it to all members. Setting `send_message` to true makes the group announcement-only. Omitted settings keep their stored value. When sending `action_signatures`, sign over the full merged settings: the stored values with this request's changes applied, not only the settings in the request.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action_signatures": [
    {
      "encoded_message_event_detail": "string",
      "message_event_signature": {
        "message_signing_key_info_list": [
          {
            "member_id": "string",
            "public_key_version": "string",
            "signing_public_key": "string"
          }
        ],
        "public_key_version": "string",
        "signature": "string",
        "signature_version": "string",
        "signing_public_key": "string"
      },
      "message_id": "string",
      "signature_payload": "string"
    }
  ],
  "add_member": true,
  "block_screen_capture": true,
  "edit_group_info": true,
  "edit_message_ttl": true,
  "send_message": true,
  "start_call": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-admin-only-settings-of-a-chat-group-conversation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the group conversation, starting with `g`.|
|body|body|[UpdateChatGroupAdminSettingsRequest](#schemaupdatechatgroupadminsettingsrequest)|true|none|
|» action_signatures|body|[[UpdateChatGroupAdminSettingsActionSignatures](#schemaupdatechatgroupadminsettingsactionsignatures)]|false|Cryptographic signatures for the action.|
|» add_member|body|boolean|false|When true, only admins can add members.|
|» block_screen_capture|body|boolean|false|When true, only admins can change screen capture blocking. Through the API, only admins can change screen capture in a group, whatever this setting says.|
|» edit_group_info|body|boolean|false|When true, only admins can edit the group name, avatar, and description.|
|» edit_message_ttl|body|boolean|false|When true, only admins can change the disappearing-message timer.|
|» send_message|body|boolean|false|When true, only admins can send messages.|
|» start_call|body|boolean|false|When true, only admins can start calls.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

## Get Chat Conversation Events, newest first; unread ones have an id above last_read_event_id

<a id="opIdgetChatConversationEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/chat/conversations/string/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/chat/conversations/{id}/events`

Retrieves the events of a specific Chat conversation, newest first, with pagination support: messages, key changes, group changes, and read receipts. Events with an id above the conversation's last_read_event_id come after the point you read up to; to collect them, page until an event's id is at or below it. Only `id` and `encoded_event` are always present. Events are either end-to-end encrypted or unencrypted, such as messages sent before the conversation was encrypted. Encrypted events carry `conversation_key_version`, and usually `conversation_token` and `message_event_signature`; treat an encrypted event without `message_event_signature` as unverified. An event without `conversation_key_version` is unencrypted. Decode each `encoded_event` client-side, and decrypt it with the conversation key named by `conversation_key_version` when that is present. A page holds up to `max_results` events and can hold fewer while `has_more` is true. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-chat-conversation-events-newest-first-unread-ones-have-an-id-above-lastreadeventid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|max_results|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of events to return.|
|pagination_token|query|string|false|The next_token from a previous response, to fetch the next page.|
|chat_message_event.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of ChatMessageEvent fields to display.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|chat_message_event.fields|conversation_id|
|chat_message_event.fields|conversation_key_version|
|chat_message_event.fields|conversation_token|
|chat_message_event.fields|created_at|
|chat_message_event.fields|encoded_event|
|chat_message_event.fields|id|
|chat_message_event.fields|is_trusted|
|chat_message_event.fields|message_event_signature|
|chat_message_event.fields|previous_id|
|chat_message_event.fields|sender_id|

```json
    {

    }
```

`POST /2/chat/conversations/{id}/invite`

Turns on the invite link for an encrypted Chat group conversation and returns the link details. The client builds the link and sends it as invite_url, in the form https://x.com/i/chat/group_join/<conversation_id>/<token>, where the token is exactly 10 letters, digits, '-' or '_'. invite_url is required when action_signatures is sent. To make the link expire, send validity_duration_msec or validity_expiry_timestamp_msec. With action_signatures, send validity_expiry_timestamp_msec, because the signed payload carries the expiry. The group name and avatar sent here are stored unencrypted and shown to anyone who opens the link.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json

            "public_key_version": "string",
            "signing_public_key": "string"
          }

        "public_key_version": "string",
        "signature": "string",
        "signature_version": "string",
        "signing_public_key": "string"
      },
      "message_id": "string",
      "signature_payload": "string"
    }
  ],
  "affiliate_user_id": "string",
  "decrypted_avatar_url": "string",
  "decrypted_title": "string",
  "invite_url": "string",
  "validity_duration_msec": "string",
  "validity_expiry_timestamp_msec": "string",
  "welcome_message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="enable-a-chat-group-invite-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the group conversation, starting with `g`.|
|body|body|[EnableChatGroupInviteRequest](#schemaenablechatgroupinviterequest)|true|none|
|» action_signatures|body|[[EnableChatGroupInviteActionSignatures](#schemaenablechatgroupinviteactionsignatures)]|false|Cryptographic signatures for the action.|
|» affiliate_user_id|body|string|false|ID of the affiliate account to associate with the link.|
|» decrypted_avatar_url|body|string|false|Group avatar URL (https) to show on the invite preview.|
|» decrypted_title|body|string|false|Group name to show on the invite preview.|
|» invite_url|body|string|false|Invite link built by the client, in the form https://x.com/i/chat/group_join/<conversation_id>/<token>, where the token is exactly 10 letters, digits, '-' or '_'. The conversation segment must match the path ID. It is part of the signed payload, so it is required when action_signatures is sent.|
|» validity_duration_msec|body|string|false|How long the link stays valid, in milliseconds, from the time of the request. With action_signatures, send validity_expiry_timestamp_msec instead.|
|» validity_expiry_timestamp_msec|body|string|false|When the link expires, in epoch milliseconds. Must be in the future. If validity_duration_msec is also sent, the two must agree within a minute.|
|» welcome_message|body|string|false|Message shown to people who open the link.|

`POST /2/chat/conversations/{id}/keys`

Adds (initializes or rotates) the encryption keys for a Chat conversation. Call this before sending messages in a new 1:1 conversation, and again with a newer key version to rotate the conversation key. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID as the conversation id; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient. The request body must contain the conversation key version and participant keys (the conversation key encrypted for each participant using their public key).

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

```json
}
```

## Send Chat Message

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/chat/conversations/string/messages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

`POST /2/chat/conversations/{id}/messages`

Sends an encrypted message to a specific Chat conversation. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient. A recipient who cannot be messaged (closed inbox, system/notification account, or a 1:1 block) returns HTTP 403 with type https://api.x.com/2/problems/recipient-not-messageable.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conversation_token": "string",
  "encoded_message_create_event": "string",
  "encoded_message_event_signature": "string",
  "message_id": "string",
  "xdk_version": "string"
}
```

|id|path|string|true|none|

|» conversation_token|body|string|false|Optional conversation token.|
|» encoded_message_create_event|body|string|true|Base64-encoded Thrift MessageCreateEvent containing encrypted message contents.|
|» encoded_message_event_signature|body|string|false|Base64-encoded Thrift MessageEventSignature for message verification.|
|» message_id|body|string|true|Unique identifier for this message.|
|» xdk_version|body|string|false|Version of the Chat XDK that produced the payload.|

`POST /2/chat/conversations/{id}/messages/delete`

Deletes one or more messages from a Chat conversation. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient. `POST /2/chat/conversations/{id}/read`

Marks a specific Chat conversation as read on behalf of the authenticated user. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient. Without action_signatures the conversation is marked read up to its newest event and the read receipt is unsigned. With one action signature over a MarkConversationReadEvent, the server sends that signed read receipt, marking the conversation read up to the event it names.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{

        "signature_version": "string",
        "signing_public_key": "string"
      },
      "message_id": "string",
      "signature_payload": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```
```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/chat/message_requests`

Retrieves the authenticated user's pending Chat message requests from one inbox. Message contents are end-to-end encrypted unless the conversation is unencrypted. Accepting or deleting requests between pages can skip or repeat requests, and a page can be empty while `next_token` is set.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

|max_results|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of message requests to return.|
|pagination_token|query|string|false|The next_token from a previous response, to fetch the next page.|
|chat_message_request.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of ChatMessageRequest fields to display.|

## Update Chat settings

<a id="opIdupdateChatSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/chat/settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_dms_from": "all",
    "always_allow_dms_from_subscribers": true,
    "av_settings": {
      "av_call_permissions": {
        "accept_calls_from_addressbook": true,
        "accept_calls_from_everyone": true,
        "accept_calls_from_following": true,
        "accept_calls_from_verified": true
      },
      "has_av_calls_enabled": true,
      "has_enhanced_call_privacy_enabled": true
    },
    "dm_quality_filter": "enabled",
    "dm_receipt_settings": "all_enabled"
  }'
```

`PUT /2/chat/settings`

Updates the authenticated user's Chat privacy settings: who can message them, read receipts, the message quality filter, and audio/video call permissions. allow_dms_from, dm_receipt_settings, and dm_quality_filter accept only their listed values, matched exactly and case-sensitively; anything else is a 400. av_settings must set at least one of its settings. Whether settings omitted from a partial av_settings keep their values or are reset is not yet confirmed; send every av_settings field you want to keep.

<a href="https://developer.x.com/">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_dms_from": "all",
  "always_allow_dms_from_subscribers": true,
  "av_settings": {
    "av_call_permissions": {
      "accept_calls_from_addressbook": true,
      "accept_calls_from_everyone": true,
      "accept_calls_from_following": true,
      "accept_calls_from_verified": true
    },
    "has_av_calls_enabled": true,
    "has_enhanced_call_privacy_enabled": true
  },
  "dm_quality_filter": "enabled",
  "dm_receipt_settings": "all_enabled"
}
```

<h3 id="update-chat-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UpdateChatSettingsRequest](#schemaupdatechatsettingsrequest)|true|none|
|» allow_dms_from|body|string|false|Who can send the user messages: `all` (anyone), `verified` (verified accounts only), or `following` (accounts the user follows).|
|» always_allow_dms_from_subscribers|body|boolean|false|Whether the user's subscribers can always message them regardless of allow_dms_from.|
|» av_settings|body|[UpdateChatSettingsAvSettings](#schemaupdatechatsettingsavsettings)|false|Audio and video call settings.|
|» dm_quality_filter|body|string|false|Low-quality message request filter: `enabled` (low-quality requests go to a separate folder) or `disabled` (all requests stay in the main inbox).|
|» dm_receipt_settings|body|string|false|Read receipts: `all_enabled` (send and receive read receipts) or `all_disabled` (neither).|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» allow_dms_from|all|
|» allow_dms_from|verified|
|» allow_dms_from|following|
|» dm_quality_filter|enabled|
|» dm_quality_filter|disabled|
|» dm_receipt_settings|all_enabled|
|» dm_receipt_settings|all_disabled|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "allow_dms_from": "all",
    "always_allow_dms_from_subscribers": true,
    "av_settings": {
      "av_call_permissions": {
        "accept_calls_from_addressbook": true,
        "accept_calls_from_everyone": true,
```

## Create Compliance Job

<a id="opIdcreateComplianceJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/compliance/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "resumable": true,
    "type": "tweets"
  }'
```

`POST /2/compliance/jobs`

## Delete DM event

<a id="opIddeleteDirectMessagesEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/dm_events/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /2/dm_events/{event_id}`

Deletes a specific direct message event by its ID, if owned by the authenticated user.

## Create Lists

<a id="opIdcreateLists"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/lists \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "private": true
  }'
```

`POST /2/lists`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "private": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-lists-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateListsRequest](#schemacreatelistsrequest)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the List (up to 100 characters).|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the List (1-25 characters).|
|» private|body|boolean|false|Whether the List is private.|

## Update List

<a id="opIdupdateLists"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/lists/1146654567674912769 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "private": true
  }'
```

`PUT /2/lists/{id}`

Updates the details of a specific List owned by the authenticated user by its ID.

<a href="https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-api/lists/manage-lists/api-reference/put-lists-id">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "private": true
}
```

|» description|body|string|false|New description for the List (up to 100 characters).|
|» name|body|string|false|New name for the List (1-25 characters).|
|» private|body|boolean|false|Whether the List is private.|

## Get Media analytics

<a id="opIdgetMediaAnalytics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/media/analytics?media_keys=string&start_time=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&end_time=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/media/analytics`

<h3 id="get-media-analytics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|media_keys|query|[string]|true|none|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|true|none|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|true|none|
|granularity|query|string|false|none|
|media_analytics.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of MediaAnalytics fields to display.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

## Upload media

<a id="opIdmediaUpload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/media/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "additional_owners": "string",
    "media": "string",
    "media_category": "tweet_image"
  }'
```

`POST /2/media/upload`

Uploads a media file for use in posts, direct messages, or ads. The response carries the media identifiers, including the media_key used to reference the asset in later calls. The media field carries the file content base64-encoded in JSON bodies (raw bytes in multipart bodies); media_category is tweet_image, tweet_video, or tweet_gif for posts and ads, dm_image/dm_video/dm_gif for DMs, or subtitles. For X Ads accounts, register the returned media_key via create_media_library_item to add it to the account's media library and use it in campaigns.

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/media/media-upload">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "additional_owners": "string",
  "media": "string",
  "media_category": "tweet_image"
}
```

<h3 id="upload-media-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[MediaUploadRequest](#schemamediauploadrequest)|true|none|
|» additional_owners|body|string|false|Comma-separated list of user IDs who can use this media.|
|» media|body|string(binary) \| string(byte)|true|The media file to upload: base64-encoded in JSON bodies, raw bytes in multipart bodies.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(binary)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string(byte)|false|none|
|» media_category|body|string|true|The category of the media being uploaded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» media_category|tweet_image|
|» media_category|tweet_video|
|» media_category|tweet_gif|

<h3 id="create-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|body|body|[CreatePostsRequest](#schemacreatepostsrequest)|true|none|
|» card_uri|body|string|false|Card URI parameter.|

|» edit_options|body|[CreatePostsEditOptions](#schemacreatepostseditoptions)|false|Edit an existing tweet rather than creating a new one.|
|» for_super_followers_only|body|boolean|false|Restrict tweet to super followers.|
|» geo|body|[CreatePostsGeo](#schemacreatepostsgeo)|false|Geo location for the tweet.|
|» made_with_ai|body|boolean|false|Disclose that the tweet contains AI-generated media.|
|» media|body|[CreatePostsMedia](#schemacreatepostsmedia)|false|Media attachments.|
|» nullcast|body|boolean|false|If true, the tweet is not shown in the public timeline.|
|» paid_partnership|body|boolean|false|Disclose that the tweet is a paid partnership.|
|» poll|body|[CreatePostsPoll](#schemacreatepostspoll)|false|Poll configuration.|
|» quote_tweet_id|body|string|false|Tweet ID to quote.|
|» reply|body|[CreatePostsReply](#schemacreatepostsreply)|false|Tweet reply configuration.|
|» reply_settings|body|string|false|Who can reply to this tweet.|
|» share_with_followers|body|boolean|false|Share an exclusive (super-follower) tweet with all followers.|
|» text|body|string|false|Text of the tweet. Required unless media is provided.  Defaulted to an empty string so it is always sent: the backend's `tweet_text` variable is non-null and rejects an absent value.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2UserToken ( Scopes: users.read tweet.read ), UserToken, BearerToken
</aside>

## Search Posts Recent

<a id="opIdsearchPostsRecent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/tweets/search/recent?query=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/search/recent`

At most one of `start_time`, `since_id` may be provided. At most one of `end_time`, `until_id` may be provided. At most one of `pagination_token`, `next_token` may be provided.

<h3 id="search-posts-recent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|true|none|
|max_results|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|next_token|query|string|false|A base32hex-encoded pagination token.|
|pagination_token|query|string|false|A base32hex-encoded pagination token.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|Must be within the last 7 days.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|none|
|since_id|query|string|false|none|
|until_id|query|string|false|none|
|sort_order|query|string|false|none|
|post.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Post fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|

## Get Posts by ID

<a id="opIdgetPostsById"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/tweets/1346889436626259968 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/{id}`

<h3 id="get-posts-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|post.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Post fields to display.|

## Get Posts Reposts


`GET /2/tweets/{id}/retweets`

## Hide reply

<a id="opIdhidePostsReply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/tweets/1346889436626259968/hidden \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "hidden": true
  }'
```

`PUT /2/tweets/{tweet_id}/hidden`

Hides or unhides a reply to a conversation owned by the authenticated user.

<a href="https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-api/tweets/hide-replies/api-reference/put-tweets-id-hidden">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "hidden": true
}
```

<h3 id="hide-reply-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tweet_id|path|[PostId](#schemapostid)|true|none|
|body|body|[HidePostsReplyRequest](#schemahidepostsreplyrequest)|true|none|
|» hidden|body|boolean|true|Whether the reply should be hidden.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "hidden": true
  },
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",

      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json

  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="hide-reply-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[HidePostsReplyResponse](#schemahidepostsreplyresponse)|
|default|Default|The request has failed.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2UserToken ( Scopes: tweet.read tweet.moderate.write users.read ), UserToken
</aside>

<h1 id="x-api-v2-spaces">Spaces</h1>

Endpoints related to retrieving, managing Spaces

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/spaces/introduction">Find out more</a>

## Get Spaces by IDs

<a id="opIdgetSpacesByIds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/spaces?ids=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/spaces`

<h3 id="get-spaces-by-ids-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|[string]|true|none|
|space.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Space fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|topic.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Topic fields to display.|

## Get Space ticket buyers

<a id="opIdgetSpacesBuyers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/spaces/string/buyers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/spaces/{id}/buyers`

Retrieves a list of Users who purchased tickets to a specific Space by its ID.

<a href="https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-api/spaces/lookup/api-reference/get-spaces-id-buyers">External documentation</a>

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2UserToken ( Scopes: users.read tweet.read space.read )
</aside>

## Get Space Posts

<a id="opIdgetSpacesPosts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/spaces/string/tweets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/spaces/{id}/tweets`

Retrieves a list of Posts shared in a specific Space by its ID.

<a href="https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-api/spaces/lookup/api-reference/get-spaces-id-tweets">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-space-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|max_results|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|pagination_token|query|string|false|A base32hex-encoded pagination token.|
|post.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Post fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|

## Activity Stream

<a id="opIdactivityStream"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/activity/stream \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/activity/stream`

Stream of X Activities

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/activity/activity-stream">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="activity-stream-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp from which the activities will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp from which the activities will be provided.|

## Stream Posts compliance data

<a id="opIdstreamPostsCompliance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/tweets/compliance/stream?partition=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/compliance/stream`

Streams all compliance data related to Posts.

<h3 id="stream-posts-compliance-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|partition|query|integer(int32)|true|The partition number.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp from which the Post Compliance events will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp from which the Post Compliance events will be provided.|

## Stream all Posts

<a id="opIdstreamPostsFirehose"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/tweets/firehose/stream?partition=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/firehose/stream`

Streams all public Posts in real-time.

<h3 id="stream-all-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|tweet.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Tweet fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|
|partition|query|integer(int32)|true|The partition number.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|

## Stream English Posts

<a id="opIdstreamPostsFirehoseEn"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/tweets/firehose/stream/lang/en?partition=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/firehose/stream/lang/en`

Streams all public English-language Posts in real-time.

<h3 id="stream-english-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|tweet.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Tweet fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|
|partition|query|integer(int32)|true|The partition number.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|

## Stream Japanese Posts

<a id="opIdstreamPostsFirehoseJa"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/tweets/firehose/stream/lang/ja?partition=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/firehose/stream/lang/ja`

Streams all public Japanese-language Posts in real-time.

<h3 id="stream-japanese-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|

|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|
|partition|query|integer(int32)|true|The partition number.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|

## Stream Portuguese Posts

<a id="opIdstreamPostsFirehosePt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/tweets/firehose/stream/lang/pt?partition=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/firehose/stream/lang/pt`

Streams all public Portuguese-language Posts in real-time.

<h3 id="stream-portuguese-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|tweet.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Tweet fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|
|partition|query|integer(int32)|true|The partition number.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|

## Stream Post labels

<a id="opIdstreamLabelsCompliance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/tweets/label/stream \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/label/stream`

Streams all labeling events applied to Posts.

<h3 id="stream-post-labels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp from which the Post labels will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp from which the Post labels will be provided.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "data": {
    "public_tweet_notice": {
      "application": "apply",
      "details": "string",
      "event_at": "2021-07-06T18:40:40.000Z",

      "extended_details_url": "string",
      "label_title": "string",
      "tweet": {
        "author_id": "2244994945",
        "id": "1346889436626259968"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

BearerToken

## Stream sampled Posts

<a id="opIdstreamPostsSample"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/tweets/sample/stream \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/sample/stream`

Streams a 1% sample of public Posts in real-time.

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/volume-streams/introduction">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="stream-sampled-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|tweet.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Tweet fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|

## Stream 10% sampled Posts

<a id="opIdstreamPostsSample10"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.x.com/2/tweets/sample10/stream?partition=1' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/sample10/stream`

Streams a 10% sample of public Posts in real-time.

<h3 id="stream-10-sampled-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|tweet.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Tweet fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|
|partition|query|integer(int32)|true|The partition number.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|

## Stream filtered Posts

<a id="opIdstreamPosts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/tweets/search/stream \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /2/tweets/search/stream`

Streams Posts in real-time matching the active rule set.

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/filtered-stream/introduction">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="stream-filtered-posts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backfill_minutes|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of minutes of backfill requested.|
|start_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The earliest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|
|end_time|query|string(date-time)|false|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The latest UTC timestamp to which the Posts will be provided.|
|tweet.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Tweet fields to display.|
|expansions|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of fields to expand.|
|media.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Media fields to display.|
|poll.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Poll fields to display.|
|user.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of User fields to display.|
|place.fields|query|[string]|false|A comma separated list of Place fields to display.|

## Update stream rules

<a id="opIdupdateRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.x.com/2/tweets/search/stream/rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "add": [
      {
        "tag": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "delete": {
      "ids": [
        "string"
      ],
      "values": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /2/tweets/search/stream/rules`

Adds or deletes rules from the active rule set for the filtered stream. Exactly one of `add`, `delete`, or `?delete_all=true` must be specified. Use `?dry_run=true` to validate without committing.

<a href="https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/filtered-stream/integrate/add-or-delete-rules">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "add": [
    {
      "tag": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "delete": {
    "ids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "values": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-stream-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dry_run|query|boolean|false|none|
|delete_all|query|boolean|false|none|
|body|body|[UpdateRulesRequest](#schemaupdaterulesrequest)|true|none|
|» add|body|[[UpdateRulesAdd](#schemaupdaterulesadd)]|false|Rules to add.|
|» delete|body|[UpdateRulesDelete](#schemaupdaterulesdelete)|false|Rules to delete by id or by value.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "tag": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "string",
      "parameter": "string",
      "resource_id": "string",
      "resource_type": "string",
      "status": 0,
      "title": "string",
      "type": "https://api.x.com/2/problems/resource-not-found",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "sent": "string",
    "summary": {}
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```
